findings.title: Call to non-existent no-arg isConditionalPasskeysEnabled() breaks compilation
findings.body: UsernameForm.authenticate() calls isConditionalPasskeysEnabled() with no arguments, but the only method defined in its superclass UsernamePasswordForm (line 160) is isConditionalPasskeysEnabled(UserModel user). There is no inherited no-arg overload, so this file will not compile. It should pass the current user, e.g. isConditionalPasskeysEnabled(context.getUser()).

findings.title: Conditional passkeys now disabled on initial login, breaking discoverable/ID-less passkey login
findings.body: isConditionalPasskeysEnabled(UserModel) now requires user != null, and authenticate() (lines 115-117) and challenge(error,field) (lines 137-139) only call webauthnAuth.fillContextForm() when it returns true. On the initial UsernamePasswordForm login page no user has been identified yet (context.getUser() == null), so the WebAuthn challenge, RP id and conditional-UI attributes are never put on the form. Previously fillContextForm() was called precisely when no user was selected, enabling discoverable credentials to identify the user. As a result the existing ID-less/passwordless flow (e.g. webauthnLoginWithDiscoverableKey in PasskeysUsernamePasswordFormTest, which expects automatic login from the first page) can no longer trigger navigator.credentials.get(), and users must enter a username/password first. The re-authentication case (user != null) should be added without removing the unauthenticated case.
